plan: Hold all patient-facing state in one public `session` dict with exactly the four contract keys, initialized from a module-level template so begin/abandon can reset it cleanly.
Copy the `appointments` sequence at construction (fresh dicts with only `id` and `label`) so caller mutation cannot affect emitted choices.

Implement `handle` as a type-dispatch table where every branch validates fully (guards for active/incomplete state and payload types) before any mutation, guaranteeing invalid actions leave accepted data untouched and never raise.

Build every screen through one `_screen(prompt, messages)` helper that attaches appointment choices exactly when the prompt is `Choose appointment` and empty lists otherwise, ensuring deterministic, freshly-allocated screen dicts.
Compute the post-correction prompt with a `_next_prompt` helper that returns the first unmet step: unconfirmed contact, then unselected appointment, then `Review and complete`.
Route all errors through `_error(reason)` producing a screen whose first message is `Error: ...` with a neutral `Error` prompt and no choices.

Implement `run_once` to check both source and sink up front (raising `RuntimeError` before calling either), then read one action, handle it, display the resulting screen exactly once, and return that same object.
Keep source and sink as plain duck-typed attributes (`read_action()` / `display(screen)`) so `unittest.mock` or hand-written standard-library fakes substitute trivially.
mechanisms: single canonical session dictionary with template-based reset
centralized deterministic screen builder with prompt-driven choice inclusion
uniform Error-screen channel for invalid and malformed actions
duck-typed injectable action source and screen sink with precondition-checked run_once
